gaps.term: Bit length of each polynomial product
gaps.quote: Each product has at most $n$ bits
gaps.note: The page asserts that every polynomial product the multiplier computes has at most n bits, but does not say how the products' sizes are set by the target's analysis or why the bound holds. The reader cannot check it from the page.

gaps.term: Total product length is O(n) and the charge sum bound
gaps.quote: which is $O(n\log n)$ when that total length is $O(n)$
gaps.note: The page gives the sum of charges as at most a constant times log n times the total product length, which assumes the multiplier's cost on an L-bit product is O(L log L). The page only states the cost for two n-bit integers and never states that the total length of the products is O(n). The reader cannot verify either premise from the page.

gaps.quote: The target's analysis is organized this way, so its running time inherits the bound.
gaps.note: This claims the target's running-time analysis charges the multiplier this way, and draws a conclusion from it. The page does not describe the target's analysis, so the reader cannot check that the target's running time inherits the bound.
